title: Altered Mental Status
hpi_narrative: {{patient_name}} presents with witnessed generalized tonic-clonic seizure: sudden loss of consciousness, tonic phase (stiffening), clonic phase (rhythmic jerking), post-ictal confusion/drowsiness. Tongue laceration and urinary incontinence are common. First unprovoked seizure requires thorough workup: CT/MRI brain (structural lesion), EEG (epileptiform discharges, classify seizure type), labs (CBC, BMP, glucose, tox screen, LP if infection suspected). Alcohol withdrawal, electrolyte abnormalities (hypoNa, hypoMg, hypoCa), hypoglycemia, and CNS infection are common triggers. Do NOT start anti-epileptic drugs after single unprovoked seizure unless high risk (abnormal EEG, structural lesion, family history). Driving restrictions per state law. If recurrent seizures or high risk → start AED (levetiracetam, lamotrigine, valproic acid). Status epilepticus: >5 min of continuous seizure or recurrent without return to baseline = medical emergency (IV lorazepam/diazepam).

stacks.label: CT/MRI brain
stacks.finding: Rule out structural lesion, hemorrhage, mass.
